title: Lithium: the lightest metal and the ion that shuttles

concepts.label: lithium: lowest E°, lightest metal
concepts.definition: Lithium has the most negative standard potential (−3.04 V) and the lowest molar mass of any metal (6.94 g/mol), so it gives the most volts and the most charge per gram (about 3860 mAh/g).

concepts.label: water stability window
concepts.definition: The 1.23 V range of electrode potentials between water's hydrogen edge (2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂) and oxygen edge (O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O); both edges shift 59 mV per tenfold change in [H⁺], and outside the window water is reduced to H₂ or oxidised to O₂ (slow gas evolution lets some cells stretch it to about 2 V).

concepts.label: non-aqueous electrolyte
concepts.definition: An electrolyte with no water: a lithium salt such as LiPF₆ (Li⁺ and PF₆⁻) dissolved in a water-free solvent whose stability window exceeds 4 V, as required by 3–4 V lithium cells.

concepts.label: lithium-metal primary cell (Li–MnO₂)
concepts.definition: A non-rechargeable cell with a lithium metal anode and a manganese dioxide cathode, Li + MnO₂ → LiMnO₂ (Mn +4 → +3), about 3 V; the CR2032 coin cell (about 225 mAh).

concepts.label: dendrite
concepts.definition: A needle of lithium metal that grows when lithium is plated during charging, because protruding spots collect more ions; it can pierce the separator and short-circuit the cell.

concepts.label: intercalation
concepts.definition: Reversible insertion of a guest ion (Li⁺) into empty seats of a solid, with the matching electron going to the solid, while the solid keeps its structure.

concepts.label: host lattice
concepts.definition: The solid framework (graphite sheets, a layered oxide, an iron phosphate framework) that provides the seats for intercalated Li⁺ and takes up or gives back the electrons.

concepts.label: graphite anode (LiC₆)
concepts.definition: The standard lithium-ion negative electrode: stacked carbon sheets that take up one lithium per six carbons, C₆ + Li⁺ + e⁻ ⇌ LiC₆, 372 mAh/g, about 0.1 V from lithium metal, swelling about 10%.

concepts.label: layered oxide cathode (LiCoO₂, LCO)
concepts.definition: A cathode host made of metal–oxygen sheets with lithium between them; in LiCoO₂ removing Li⁺ raises cobalt from +3 towards +4 and only about half the lithium can be removed reversibly (about 140 mAh/g, cell about 3.7 V, 4.2 V full).

concepts.label: rocking-chair mechanism
concepts.definition: The working principle of a lithium-ion cell: the same Li⁺ ions shuttle between two host lattices (graphite and a cathode host) through the electrolyte while electrons take the wire; lithium stays +1 and the hosts do the redox.

concepts.label: NMC (mixed layered oxide)
concepts.definition: LiNiₓMnᵧCo_zO₂, a layered oxide in which most cobalt is replaced by nickel (which does most of the redox) and manganese (which stays +4 and stabilises); about 3.7 V and roughly 160–200 usable mAh/g.

concepts.label: LFP (LiFePO₄)
concepts.definition: Lithium iron phosphate, a non-layered phosphate framework cathode: LiFePO₄ ⇌ FePO₄ + Li⁺ + e⁻ (Fe +2 ⇌ +3), 170 mAh/g theoretical, a flat cell voltage near 3.3 V, cheap, long-lived and the safest common cathode.

concepts.label: SEI layer
concepts.definition: The solid electrolyte interphase: a nanometre-thin film of lithium salts formed on graphite during the first charge by reduction of the electrolyte; it conducts Li⁺ but blocks electrons, so it stops further breakdown, at the cost of 5–10% of the lithium and slow capacity fade.

summary: Running example: 0.100 mol of lithium (0.694 g, 2.68 Ah), the counterpart of the 6.54 g zinc strip, followed from bare metal (CR2032 Li–MnO₂ coin cell, dendrites on recharge) into a graphite host (7.21 g of carbon, LiC₆, 372 mAh/g) and a cathode host (LCO 19.6 g, NMC, LFP). A reusable cell picture shows 12 lithium dots moving one at a time through the electrolyte while electrons take the wire; the water stability window is drawn on the potential ladder with Nernst-shifted edges. Capstone: a rocking-chair simulator with switchable cathode (LCO / NMC / LFP), voltage read from host fill level (simplified curves), energy stored, a protection circuit that can be turned off to overcharge into lithium plating; later lessons can reuse the ideal voltage-vs-state-of-charge curves (no resistance yet) and the usable mAh/g figures.
